  <instructions>
You are executing one bead in an isolated DDx execution worktree. The bead's <description> and <acceptance> are the contract: every AC must be provably satisfied by a specific code, test, or file after your commit.

## Step 0: size check

Too big if any holds:

- More than ~6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems.
- AC mixes design, implementation, integration tests, and docs.
- Description names multiple feature-sized pieces.
- More than ~500 lines across ~5+ files in unrelated packages.
- If the bead description exceeds 8000 bytes, use a split-first pass.
- Auto-decomposition is capped at depth 2: root beads may split once, children once more; reject third-level splits with an explanation.

If too big, decompose:

1. `ddx bead create` for each child (copy parent's labels and spec-id).
2. `ddx bead dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` to record edges.
3. `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'`.
4. Write `no_changes_rationale.txt` under the bead metadata `bundle` path with child IDs, then stop.

Decomposition alone is success. Do not mix it with implementation.

## How to work

- Read first. If the bead names files, specs, or prior beads, read them before editing — do not guess.
- Cross-reference each AC to concrete evidence (test, file, function) before committing. If you cannot point at it, it is not done.
- Run the project's test and lint commands before committing. **Do not commit red code** — fix failures first.
- Run git/index mutations sequentially; do not use parallel tool calls for `git add`, `git commit`, or other staging/commit commands.
- Stage with `git add <specific-paths>`; never `git add -A` (the worktree may have unrelated WIP).
- If `lefthook run pre-commit` depends on staged files, rerun it after staging the exact commit set. A `no-staged-files` run is not acceptance evidence.
- Commit exactly once when green; conventional-commit subject ending with `[<bead-id>]`. Stop after the commit.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's scope.
- Current-bead lifecycle is orchestrator-owned. Do not run `ddx bead update <bead-id> --claim`, `ddx bead update <bead-id> --status <status>`, `ddx bead update <bead-id> --unclaim`, or `ddx bead close <bead-id>`. Step 0 still allows `ddx bead create`, `ddx bead dep add`, and `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'`.
- If you cannot finish, write `no_changes_rationale.txt` under the bead metadata `bundle` path before exiting. No commit or rationale ⇒ DDx records `no_evidence_produced`.

## no_changes contract

The `no_changes_rationale.txt` file under the bead metadata `bundle` path must contain one of:

- `verification_command: <cmd>` — repo cwd; exit 0 closes, nonzero rejects.
- `status: open` + `reason: <retryable>` — open, smart retry.
- `status: proposed` + `reason: <operator needed>` — operator lane.
- `status: blocked` + `reason: <external blocker>` — blocked lane.

No pseudo-statuses. Bare rationales and `status: needs_investigation` are rejected.

For orchestrator decomposition, add `orchestrator_action: decompose` alongside `status: open`.

## Reports

Reports go under the bead metadata `bundle` path in `.ddx/executions/`. **Never write reports to `/tmp` or outside the repo**. Use a named in-repo path when given; otherwise write `<short-name>.md` there. Commit it with the code.

## Mode and overrides

DDX_MODE=bead_execution: edit code/docs for bead AC. Only broad queue-steward default is overridden; tracker, merge-policy, verification, safety stay active. Bead description/AC override CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and defaults.

## Review gate

- The review is a gate, not an escape hatch — meet every AC in this pass.
- Address every BLOCKING `<review-findings>` item; do not declare `no_changes` with blocking findings open.

## Constraints

- Work only inside this execution worktree.
- Keep `.ddx/executions/` intact — DDx uses it as execution evidence.
- **Never run `ddx init`** — the workspace is initialized.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's named scope.
- Do not rewrite CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other instruction files unless the bead asks.

## When the work is done

After the commit succeeds and every AC is verified, stop. Return control to the orchestrator.
  </instructions>
  <bead id="fizeau-e633cd36">
    <title>providers/llamaserver: nest enable_thinking inside chat_template_kwargs envelope</title>
    <description>
PROBLEM: ADR-010 amendment (2026-05-11) §8'-9' requires llamaserver to send `enable_thinking` inside a `chat_template_kwargs` envelope, matching upstream llama.cpp expectations. Current code emits `enable_thinking` at the top level of the request body, which llama.cpp ignores.

ROOT CAUSE: internal/provider/llamaserver request-body builder (locate via `grep -rn 'enable_thinking' internal/provider/llamaserver`) sets `enable_thinking` as a sibling of model/messages instead of nesting it under `chat_template_kwargs`.

PROPOSED FIX: In the llamaserver request-body construction path, replace the top-level `enable_thinking` field with a `chat_template_kwargs` object whose `enable_thinking` member carries the boolean. Remove the obsolete top-level field. Add an assertion test `TestLlamaserver_EnableThinking_WireBody` that marshals a request with thinking enabled and asserts (a) `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking == true`, (b) no top-level `enable_thinking` key exists.

NON-SCOPE: ThinkingWireFormatOpenAIEffort enum addition (separate child); reasoning-token telemetry fallback (separate child); changes to llamaserver auth, streaming, or error mapping; refactors to shared request-body helpers beyond the minimal change.

Governing artifacts: ADR-010 amendment 2026-05-11 §8'-9'; AR-2026-05-17-repo; source review fizeau-8e37e536.

VERIFICATION: `go test ./internal/provider/llamaserver/... ./... -count=1` green; lefthook hooks pass.

AC:
1) llamaserver request body emits `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`; no top-level `enable_thinking` key remains.
2) Test `TestLlamaserver_EnableThinking_WireBody` asserts both the presence of the nested key and absence of the top-level key.
3) Test `TestLlamaserver_EnableThinking_Disabled` asserts the envelope is omitted (or `enable_thinking:false` nested) when thinking is disabled, matching ADR-010 §9'.
4) `go test ./... -count=1` passes.
5) lefthook hooks pass.
    </description>
    <acceptance>
1) llamaserver request body nests enable_thinking inside chat_template_kwargs.
2) TestLlamaserver_EnableThinking_WireBody asserts nested-present and top-level-absent.
3) TestLlamaserver_EnableThinking_Disabled covers the disabled path per ADR-010 §9'.
4) go test ./... -count=1 green.
5) lefthook pre-commit and pre-push pass.
    </acceptance>

The llamaserver wire path was already using the nested `chat_template_kwargs` envelope in the shared OpenAI serializer, so I added provider-specific regression tests rather than changing production code.

- Added [internal/provider/llamaserver/enable_thinking_test.go](/var/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-e633cd36-20260518T145935-d642b262/internal/provider/llamaserver/enable_thinking_test.go#L20-L90) with `TestLlamaserver_EnableThinking_WireBody` and `TestLlamaserver_EnableThinking_Disabled`.
- The helper spins up a fake llamaserver, calls `llamaserver.New(...).Chat(...)`, and asserts `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` is present while top-level `enable_thinking` is absent. The disabled case asserts the nested `enable_thinking:false` form, which matches ADR-010 §9'.
- `go test ./internal/provider/llamaserver/... -count=1` passed.
- `lefthook run pre-commit` passed after staging just the new test file.
- `go test ./... -count=1` failed in unrelated baseline areas outside this bead, including `service_aliveness_test.go`, `agentcli/cli_process_test.go`, `cmd/bench`, and `internal/harnesses`, so the repo-wide gate and pre-push are not green in this environment.
- I wrote the blocker note at [.ddx/executions/20260518T145935-d642b262/no_changes_rationale.txt](/var/tmp/ddx-exec-wt/.execute-bead-wt-fizeau-e633cd36-20260518T145935-d642b262/.ddx/executions/20260518T145935-d642b262/no_changes_rationale.txt#L1-L2).
